items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: And of course I liked — who was this guy, Tab Smith?

ctx.x: Who do you name as your basic influences or people that you looked up to on the saxophone?

Well you can’t speak about the alto saxophone unless you say Charlie Parker, Bird Parker. At the time when — I saw Bird one time, in that 767 when he came in there when he had some union problem see. You know he wasn’t concerned about a union card or whatever, but he came to Los Angeles and he didn’t have his union card, and the Mr. Elmer Thane said, “Oh you can’t play” blah-blah-blah-blah-blah. And he came and I was working there that day, and he asked Florence, “Florence, please ask Thane to give me my card.”…
